evidence.note: Explicit ordered milestone plan established: (1) Cargo.toml as binary+deps, (2) main.rs LSP skeleton, (3) test basic compilation, (4) build handlers then test. Correctly sequences transport/handshake (initialize/shutdown skeleton) before parser before per-method work.

Layered decomposition made explicit: 'Examine golden patterns per method → implement Java AST analysis via tree-sitter → implement each LSP method handler → build and test.' This is the transport→AST→per-method dependency order.

After first full-suite run, builds a per-method scoreboard (documentSymbol 1.5%, foldingRange 0%, hover 18.7%, selectionRange 0%, prepareCallHierarchy 0%, semanticTokens 0%, references 21.8%) and explicitly prioritizes 'the most failing methods' — using test payoff to order handler work.

Deliberate deferral of low-value complexity: notes semanticTokens 'accounts for only 0.088% of tests', explicitly choosing to prioritize foldingRange/references over it — weight-based prioritization to maximize passing tests.

Late-stage decomposition still tracked as ordered per-method targets with pass-rate exit criteria (foldingRange 75.5%, references 85.6%, hover 91.4%...), showing sustained milestone structure across the horizon, though final steps drift into repetitive 'wait for test' plans.

reasoning: The agent maintained an explicit ordered plan that correctly sequenced transport → parser/AST → per-method handlers (steps 13-24), used compilation and per-method golden pass-rates as concrete done-checks, and prioritized handler work by test impact — even deferring semanticTokens as low-value (0.088% of tests). This matches anchor 8 strongly, with touches of 10 (weight-based deferral, adapting focus to which methods matter). It falls short of a full 10 because prioritization was largely reactive to observed failures rather than an upfront frequency ranking, and late-stage plans became repetitive/thrashy rather than crisply milestone-gated.
